claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting alloy has suboptimal strength and plasticity for the intended application.
A post-solidification thermal aging treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The aging treatment will form fine, coherent precipitates dispersed within the lamellar matrix.
The induced precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The induced precipitates will redistribute local stresses.
Precipitate-induced obstruction of dislocation motion and stress redistribution will increase yield strength.
The precipitates will improve resistance to room-temperature creep.
Precipitation aging may activate mechanisms that improve ductility.
The precipitates will contribute to a more stable microstructure.
Aging-induced changes in local chemistry and passivation behavior may improve corrosion resistance.
Relative to the as-solidified lamellar alloy, the aged alloy is expected to have higher yield strength.
Relative to the as-solidified lamellar alloy, the aged alloy is expected to have improved plasticity.
Relative to the as-solidified lamellar alloy, the aged alloy is expected to have enhanced creep resistance.
Relative to the as-solidified lamellar alloy, the aged alloy is expected to have enhanced corrosion performance.
The aged alloy will be better suited for fasteners exposed to severe thermal, mechanical, creep, and corrosive service conditions.
The intervention is applicable from near-cryogenic to elevated temperatures and under fastener-relevant loads and corrosive environments.
There may be a trade-off between precipitation strengthening and retention of ductility.
